scene.title: Why the Sky Is Blue
scene.subtitle: Air molecules scatter short wavelengths more than long ones

answer.headline: The sky looks blue because air molecules scatter the short, blue wavelengths of sunlight far more strongly than the longer red and yellow ones.
body: Sunlight looks white, but it is a mix of every color in the visible spectrum. As that light passes through the atmosphere, it collides with tiny nitrogen and oxygen molecules. This is called Rayleigh scattering, and it scatters shorter wavelengths, like blue and violet, roughly ten times more strongly than longer wavelengths like red. Our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet, so the sky reads as blue rather than violet.

facts: Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red light.
Shorter wavelengths scatter more off small molecules.
